records.title: Add the per-kind watcher configuration, the reflector stores, and the InitDone atomic swap
records.body:
## Summary

Add `Store<V>`, the per-kind reflector store with tombstones and an atomic staging swap at
`Event::InitDone`, plus `watch_config(kind)`, the decided `watcher::Config` for every watched kind, plus
`apply_event`, the one function in this crate that is allowed to match on a `watcher::Event` variant.
Resync is zero and there is no option to change it. There is no `StoreUpdater` type: the updater is the
pair of free functions `apply_event` and `apply_meta_event` plus `spawn_kind`, and `watch/stores.rs` is
the module the `no-event-variant-branch` lint exempts by exact path.

## Context

This issue owns the milestone's central invariant:

> **INVARIANT L1.** No code in `irontraffic-k8s` may branch on the *variant* of a `watcher::Event` to
> decide what the world looks like. `Apply`, `Delete`, `InitApply` and `InitDone` may only update the
> store and mark dirty. All decisions are made by reading the store.

kube-rs's `watcher::Event` is `Apply(K) | Delete(K) | Init | InitApply(K) | InitDone`
(`kube-runtime/src/watcher.rs:55-84`). The documentation on `InitDone` says it "can be used as a signal
to replace buffered store contents atomically" and that "Any objects that were previously `Applied` but
are not listed in any of the `InitApply` events should be assumed to have been `Deleted`". The `Delete`
variant carries the source warning: "This should not be used for managing persistent state elsewhere,
since events may be lost if the watcher is unavailable. Use Finalizers instead." That warning, written by
the library authors, is the whole edge-triggered-is-a-bug argument.

Why edge-triggered logic is a defect, in this system's terms:

1. **Events are lost.** A watch that dies and relists after an HTTP 410 Gone (an etcd compaction)
   delivers `Init` / `InitApply*` / `InitDone` with no delete events for the objects that vanished while
   we were disconnected. An edge-triggered handler leaks those routes into the data plane forever. A
   level-triggered one recomputes and they are gone.
2. **Events are coalesced.** Our own scheduler collapses a create-then-delete inside the debounce window
   into nothing at all. Correct for level, catastrophic for edge.
3. **Events across kinds have no relative order.** A route can arrive before its Gateway, its Service,
   its EndpointSlice and its ReferenceGrant, in any permutation. Edge logic must then encode a state
   machine per arrival order; level logic has one code path.
4. **Restarts.** A controller that restarts has seen no events at all and must be correct immediately.

Decided watch parameters, from `kube-runtime/src/watcher.rs:212-280`:

- `bookmarks: true`, the kube-rs default, never disabled. The documentation says it "should generally not
  be turned off".
- `initial_list_strategy: ListWatch` with `page_size: Some(500)` by default, matching client-go's pager
  default. `StreamingList` is offered behind `k8s.streamingLists=true` because it requires the
  server-side watch-list feature and we must not hard-depend on it.
- `list_semantic`: the default `MostRecent` for the initial list of every kind, because a stale initial
  list of Gateways can make us tombstone routes incorrectly.
- `timeout`: the kube-rs default of 290 seconds, capped at 295.
- **`resync` is zero and no configuration key exposes it.** A nonzero informer resync period re-delivers
  every cached object to every handler on a timer, producing a synchronised burst of `n` reconciles. It
  exists to paper over missed events; the right fix is that reconciliation is level triggered and
  idempotent. Eventual consistency comes from bookmarks, the level-triggered recompute, and the bounded
  periodic full re-translation in `{{k8s-worldview-and-coalescer}}`.
- `DefaultBackoff` (`watcher.rs:978-988`) is `ResetTimerBackoff::new(ExponentialBackoff::new(800ms, 30s,
  2.0, jitter=true), 120s)`, taken from client-go's reflector. Reuse it; do not invent new numbers.

The selector table, decided per kind:

| Kind | Scope | Selector | Projection |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GatewayClass | cluster | none | full view |
| Gateway | cluster wide | none | full view, tombstone if the class is not ours |
| ListenerSet | cluster wide | none | full view, tombstone if the parent Gateway is not ours |
| HTTPRoute, GRPCRoute, TLSRoute, TCPRoute, UDPRoute | cluster wide | none | full view, tombstone if no parentRef resolves to an owned Gateway |
| ReferenceGrant | cluster wide | none | full view |
| BackendTLSPolicy | cluster wide | none | full view |
| Ingress | cluster wide | none | full view, tombstone if the IngressClass is not ours |
| IngressClass | cluster | none | full view |
| Service | cluster wide | none | ports, type, appProtocol, trafficDistribution |
| EndpointSlice | cluster wide | none | addresses, conditions, zone, nodeName, hints, ports; tombstone if `kubernetes.io/service-name` is not referenced |
| Node | cluster | none | `metadata_watcher`, metadata only |
| Namespace | cluster | none | `metadata_watcher`, metadata only: labels alone |
| Secret | per object | `field_selector: metadata.name=<name>` in one namespace | never in this issue |

Namespace is on that list because `allowedRoutes.namespaces.from: Selector` evaluates a
`metav1.LabelSelector` against the Namespace object's labels, and labels are metadata. It is a Core
support level feature, so it cannot be dropped, and there is no other source for those labels. Like
Node, it is watched metadata-only, so the cost is a few hundred bytes per namespace.

**Consumers, and what this issue deliberately leaves unwired.** When this merges, `spawn_kind` has no
caller: nothing constructs a `kube::Client`, nothing starts a task, and the `irontraffic` binary still
has no dependency on this crate. That is correct and it is not an oversight. `Stores` is read by
`k8s-worldview-and-coalescer` (#296), which builds `WorldView<'a>` over it and is the first consumer of
`DirtyFlag::take`; `spawn_kind` is first called by `k8s-controller-loops-and-con

records.title: feat(pgparser): implement CTE (WITH [RECURSIVE]) support
records.body:
Parent: 76
Depends on: #82, #83, #84, #85 (all DML statement kinds — INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, set operations)

## Summary

Implement `WITH [RECURSIVE] with_query [, ...]` support as a leading clause on `SELECT`/`INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`/set-operation statements.

## Why this comes after the individual DML parsers, not alongside SELECT

PostgreSQL's CTE bodies can be `SELECT`, `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, or (later) `MERGE` — e.g. `WITH deleted AS (DELETE FROM logs WHERE ... RETURNING *) INSERT INTO archive SELECT * FROM deleted` is a normal, common pattern. MySQL's `WITH` (already in `sqlfmt/parser`) only ever wraps a `SELECT`, so this is real additional scope, not a port — hence its own issue, sequenced after 82/83/84/85 exist to be wrapped.

## Grammar (PG13+ baseline; see [official WITH docs](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/queries-with.html))

```
WITH [ RECURSIVE ] cte_name [ ( column [, ...] ) ] AS [ [ NOT ] MATERIALIZED ] ( select | insert | update | delete )
    [, ...]
```

## Scope for this issue

- `WITH`/`WITH RECURSIVE`, multiple comma-separated CTEs, optional column-name list.
- CTE bodies: `SELECT` (incl. set-operation chains), `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`.
- `[NOT] MATERIALIZED` hint.
- Wire `WITH` as an optional leading clause on `ParseSelect`, `ParseInsert`, `ParseUpdate`, `ParseDelete`, and the set-operation parser.

## Deferred (not this issue)

- `MERGE` as a CTE body (depends on 87, which depends on this issue — see the epic's dependency order).
- `SEARCH { BREADTH | DEPTH } FIRST BY ...` and `CYCLE ...` clauses on recursive CTEs — PG14+, low usage, own follow-up.

## Requirements

- Table-driven tests, including a DML-body CTE feeding another DML statement (the pattern above).

records.title: contract(editor-intelligence): declare exact external substrate dependencies per claim row
records.body:
Parent/controller: #7460
Feeds: compiler-profile claim join #12200 and future external substrate joins
Coordinates: #7430 / #4245 / #6731 / #3099

## One-PR outcome

Extend the machine claim-definition contract behind the editor-intelligence matrix with typed, versioned external-substrate dependencies. For each applicable user-facing claim row, declare exactly which external status/profile/rail rows are prerequisites, how subjects and currentness join, how limitations/nonclaims propagate, and how the combined claim ceiling is derived. Emit a checked contract equivalent to:

```text
editor_intelligence_external_dependency.v1
```

This PR defines dependency declarations, validation and deterministic projections only. It does not consume `compiler_profile_status.v1`, implement #12200, select current external status, change focused feature/provider behavior, generate a new final claim matrix, or grant support/release/publication authority.

## Dependency declaration

For every declared external dependency retain at least:

```text
dependency ID/version/semantic identity
owning editor claim ID/version and exact subject
external source family/schema and validator identity
required external profile/rail ID/version/semantic identity
required external row IDs and dispositions
external subject selector and exact relation to the editor claim subject
source/process/package/install/client/platform/root/series/fact/effect stage relation
currentness and invalidation inputs
allowed external result states
limitation/nonclaim propagation law
combined blocker/owner/wake-event law
claim-ceiling composition law
history/supersession relation
```

A dependency is exact policy. It is not inferred from implementation proximity, package/crate/path, issue links, feature names, shared entities, method names, provider names, comments or current passing output.

## Applicability and selection law

- only checked claim definitions may declare a dependency;
- every dependency binds an exact claim row and exact source row set;
- required, conditional, optional, unsupported and not-applicable dependency dispositions remain explicit;
- conditional dependencies require complete selector inputs; missing selector state is not silently unselected;
- a claim with no declared external dependency remains governed by its existing focused evidence;
- one broad profile/rail cannot be attached to all editor claims by default;
- dependency declarations cannot be added or removed after observing candidate results without a version transition;
- unlanded source schema/row authority remains an explicit unresolved dependency, not a prose placeholder or omitted field.

## Subject and stage relation

Represent exact allowed relations equivalent to:

```text
same repository/source candidate
explicit source→package→process→client derivation
same project/root/configuration subject
same provider/fact/edit class
same platform/client where selected
same profile/series/toolchain where selected
```

Rules:

- same name, output, URI, version text, path, package spelling or issue relation is not subject equality;
- one claim/client/platform/root/series/fact/effect/stage cannot satisfy another;
- source/process/package/install/client stages remain distinct;
- one external row cannot fill another’s missing subject dimensions;
- an exact directional derivation must come from the source contract; the claim dependency cannot invent it;
- historical/stale/invalid/absent/conflicting source state cannot become current through the dependency relation.

## Result composition law

Keep independent:

```text
external substrate/profile/rail result
canonical fact/service implementation
provider consumption and external response
edit authorization
independent edit application
representative project proof
installed actual-client application
public claim ceiling
```

A dependency declaration must specify which external states permit the editor claim to remain eligible. At minimum:

- external `pass` may satisfy only the declared substrate prerequisite;
- external `pass_with_declared_limitations` propagates every applicable limitation/nonclaim and lowers the combined ceiling;
- external failed/not-proven/stale/invalid/absent/conflicting state blocks only the dependent claim rows;
- one external pass never manufactures focused feature/provider/edit/client evidence;
- focused feature/provider/client pass never manufactures external profile/rail closure;
- optional/conditional/unsupported/not-applicable cannot satisfy a required dependency;
- performance or aggregate score cannot substitute for correctness/currentness;
- no score, percentage, traffic light or majority rule composes the planes.

## Claim-ceiling composition

Derive the maximum combined wording as the intersection of:

```text
editor claim/focused row ceiling
external profile/rail and required-row ceilings
source and authority tier
provider/edit/application state
representative and installed-host stage
client/platform/root/series/fact/effect scope
all propagated limitations/nonclaims
```

Rules:

- the combined wording is no broader than the narrowest source plane;
- one selected profile/client/platform/fact class cannot become “all”;
- parser/compiler-internal proof cannot become editor behavior;
- installed-client evidence cannot repair failed substrate or provider behavior;
- allowed limitations/nonclaims remain visible in machine and human projections;
- support/release/publication authority remains false/empty and outside this dependency contract.

## Checked manifest and tooling

Add exact schema/model/validation and commands equivalent to:

```bash
cargo xtask semantic-scorecard dependencies check
cargo xtask semantic-scorecard dependencies explain <claim-id>
```

The checked dependency data lives with the canonical claim-definition authority selected during implementation. Do not maintain a second hand-copied dependency list inside #12200 or generated Markdown.

`check` validates:

```text
claim a

records.title: integration(compiler-profile): consume coherent generations in editor-intelligence and product-health joins
records.body:
Parent/controller: #12437
Coherent current-generation view: #12438
Current status/read adapter: #12443
Editor-intelligence join authority: #12362 / #12200 / #7460
Product-health rail authority: #12359 / #12201 / #3058
Machine compiler-profile status: #12351
Claim-ceiling verification: #12393
Packet enrollment/integrity: #12429 / #12420

## One-PR outcome

Make the **current** editor-intelligence and product-health consumers obtain compiler-profile dependency/rail truth from the exact #12200 and #12201 packet members contained in one coherent #12438 current generation, with an exact relation to that generation's #12351 machine-status member.

The #12200/#12201 producer semantics remain unchanged and continue to build join/rail packets before generation assembly. This PR owns the current-generation adapters and downstream currentness binding only. It does not infer dependencies, re-run the joins, re-evaluate compiler profiles, modify focused feature/client evidence, create a score, or grant support/release/publication authority.

## Current join boundary

```text
#12438 coherent current generation
├─ exact compiler_profile_status.v1 member
├─ exact editor-intelligence join member from #12200
└─ exact product-health rail member from #12201
        ↓
current #7460 / #3058 machine and generated consumers
```

All three members must belong to the same exact generation/profile/candidate/current-selection/status dependency closure. One current member cannot be paired with a loose or historical sibling.

## Editor-intelligence adapter law

- Consume only the exact checked dependency rows declared by #12362 and the exact #12200 result member.
- Preserve compiler substrate and focused feature/provider/edit/client planes independently.
- A passing compiler profile satisfies only the explicitly declared substrate dependency.
- Compiler pass cannot manufacture canonical facts, provider behavior, edit authorization/application, representative-project behavior, installed-client behavior or support.
- Focused feature/client pass cannot manufacture compiler-profile closure.
- Current failed/not-proven/stale/invalid/absent/conflicting compiler dependency blocks only exact dependent rows; unrelated rows remain unchanged.
- Every propagated limitation, nonclaim, stage and subject ceiling remains visible.
- Missing required current join member is explicit unavailable/not-proven; the consumer cannot recompute or infer it from names/issues/files.

## Product-health adapter law

- Consume the exact #12201 rail packet contained in the generation and validate its #12351 status source identity.
- Every maintained profile remains an independent named rail.
- Lower profiles cannot satisfy stronger profiles.
- Compiler rails cannot satisfy parser, editor-client, formatter, DAP, packaging, security, performance, CI, release-artifact or another area.
- Another area cannot satisfy a compiler rail.
- Missing/stale/invalid/absent/conflicting compiler source remains an explicit rail state; the rail cannot disappear.
- No score, percentage, traffic light, maturity level, majority or “mostly ready” result may replace named rails.
- Performance cannot compensate for incorrect/stale profile truth.

## Currentness and history

- Capture one #12438 view per downstream assembly/read operation.
- Validate join/rail packet generation, profile, candidate, current-selection and status-source identities.
- Current red/not-proven/stale/invalid/absence/conflict has no affirmative dependent wording.
- Historical pass or historical join/rail packets cannot supply current dependencies.
- A status movement without a matching new join/rail member makes the generation invalid or non-current under #12413; consumers cannot retain the prior join.
- A join/rail renderer-only movement remains presentation-bound and cannot change source status truth.
- Issue/PR/check/docs state is navigation only.

## Consumer surfaces

Migrate current exact equivalents of:

```text
semantic-scorecard/editor-intelligence current claim assembly
editor-intelligence generated machine/human projections
product-health current source adapter and assembler input
product-health current show/diff/generated view
any current compiler-profile claim/rail registry import
```

Fixture/producer tests may continue to invoke #12200/#12201 over explicit input packets. Repository-current consumption uses the coherent generation.

## Falsifiers first

Tests fail when deliberately:

1. combines current status with a join or rail from another generation;
2. selects a loose/newer/greener join or rail packet;
3. lets historical compiler pass/join/rail satisfy current claims;
4. lets compiler-profile pass promote every feature/provider/client row;
5. lets focused feature/client pass satisfy compiler-profile closure;
6. blocks an unrelated feature with no declared compiler dependency;
7. hides a limitation/nonclaim/stale state or widens the claim ceiling;
8. lets lower profile satisfy a stronger profile;
9. collapses source/process/package/install/client or static/EIR/provider/edit/client stages;
10. lets one client/platform/root/series/fact/effect become all;
11. lets compiler rail fill another health area or another area fill compiler;
12. lets performance/score/majority override correctness/currentness;
13. omits a declared rail or dependency because the current packet is missing;
14. recomputes dependencies from issue links, file paths, method names or output;
15. retains prior join/rail after source status movement;
16. changes output under input/completion/map ordering;
17. leaks raw source, receipts, paths, environment, credentials or unbounded errors;
18. mutates source status/profile/product behavior or sets support/release/publication authority.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Current editor-intelligence and product-health consumers capture one coherent current generation.
- [ ] Compiler status, editor join and product-health rail members share exact generation/profile/candidate/current-selec

Tracking: V1.0 implementation — operator ceiling + instrumentation + cancellation propagation (RFC #2251)
records.body:
Tracking issue for V1.0 implementation of the platform deadline architecture (RFC #2251). Scope is V1.0 only — V1.5 (heartbeat phase tracking) and V2 (quality envelope + continueAsNew) have separate tracking issues filed once V1.0 lands.

## Pre-V1.0 gates (must close before any V1.0 implementation merges)

- [ ] **Reproduce or hedge Issue 4** — run `scripts/measure-coordinator-task-bounds.sh` (PR #2254) against staging. Capture JSON output + heartbeat trace. Decision: V1.0 either ships against a confirmed bug ("fixes Issue 4") or as defensive infra ("prophylactic for the agent-hang class; Issue 4 root cause unresolved"). Either is acceptable; ambiguity is not.
- [ ] **Instrumentation deliverable spec'd** (this is what makes V1.0 self-bootstrapping — see RFC §"Bootstrap path"). Specifically:
  - Registry table schema reviewed (proposed: `task_executions` with `(task_id, skill_id, adapter_name, status, started_at, completed_at, ceiling_secs_at_start)`; see "V1.0 Instrumentation" below)
  - Index strategy reviewed for the recompute query path
- [ ] **Per-adapter cancellation matrix audit** — owned by adapter team. Tracking issue filed separately; V1.0 implementation merges only after the matrix is populated for the four native adapters at minimum (claude-code, hermes, langchain, crewai). Subprocess adapters (codex, ollama, gemini-cli) audited as part of the deprecation track.

## V1.0 deliverables

### Operator ceiling enforcement

- [ ] `MAX_TASK_EXECUTION_SECS` env-tunable per skill/workspace (placeholder defaults: **900s sync, 24h async**; rationale per RFC §"Bootstrap path")
- [ ] SIGTERM-at-ceiling + 30s grace + SIGKILL pipeline in the runtime
- [ ] `cleanup_grace_secs` per-adapter override field on `RuntimeCapabilities` (#117 dataclass already exists; just needs the field + plumbing)
- [ ] Async-task ceiling: `delegate_task_async` rejects requests with no ceiling or `ceiling > 24h`
- [ ] Platform wraps post-SIGTERM response with `quality: "terminated"` envelope value (the schema-validator gate that hard-rejects agent-authored `terminated` is V2 work, but the platform-side wrap ships at V1.0)

### Per-task duration instrumentation (the bootstrap data source)

- [ ] Migration: new `task_executions` table OR new event type on `activity_logs` (RFC says `activity_logs.event_type='task_executed'` for unified audit; team to confirm — pick one and document why)
- [ ] Write path: every task transition (start, completion, failure, abandonment, termination) emits a row/event with at minimum `(task_id, skill_id, adapter_name, status, started_at, completed_at)` plus the ceiling that was in effect at task start (so the recompute can EXCLUDE terminated tasks whose duration ≈ ceiling — slow-skill ratchet protection)
- [ ] Backfill strategy: not required (V1.0 ships fresh; no pre-existing data to reconstruct)

### Cancellation propagation

- [ ] Parent's adapter emits `cancel_delegated_tasks(parent_task_id)` A2A control message during its 30s grace
- [ ] Platform looks up active children in `delegations` table (already exists post-#302), sends SIGTERM to each
- [ ] Bounded retry: 3 attempts, exponential backoff up to 30s
- [ ] 90s child-unreachable timeout → mark delegation `abandoned`, audit-log orphan, hand off to org_purges-style retry sweeper
- [ ] No SLO baked into the spec — observed propagation latency captured in instrumentation, surfaced in dashboards, SLO derived from 30 days of data (per RFC §"Consistency model")

### Cancellation audit trail

- [ ] `activity_logs.event_type='task_terminated'` with the structured JSON payload from RFC §V1.0 step 6 — `termination_reason`, `terminator_workspace_id`, `propagation_attempts`, `orphan_descendants`, `graph_depth`, `total_propagation_secs`
- [ ] No new `task_terminations` table — premature optimization per RFC §"What was rejected"

### Envelope observability (NOT enforcement)

- [ ] Every skill response parsed for envelope schema compliance
- [ ] Per-(skill, adapter) compliance metric exposed: `envelope_compliance_rate = compliant_responses / total_responses`
- [ ] Drift alert when `compliance_rate < 50%` on any skill
- [ ] No enforcement at V1.0 — just measurement. V2 enforcement gates on >80% compliance per skill (evidence-based).

### `caller_disconnected` signal

- [ ] When caller-deadline expires while operator ceiling still has time: worker finishes current tool call, persists result by `task_id`, exits cleanly
- [ ] Result retrievable by `task_id` later; not pushed
- [ ] HTTP/2 RST_STREAM + gRPC `Context.Done()` semantics

### Recompute job (the loop-closer)

- [ ] Sweeper runs daily; populates per-(skill, adapter) ceiling registry from instrumentation data
- [ ] First measurement-driven run fires **30 days post-V1.0-ship** — until then, all skills run under placeholder defaults
- [ ] Auto-decrease only: `min(prior_ceiling, max(900s, observed_p99 * 1.5))` — ceilings ratchet DOWN with measurement, never UP automatically
- [ ] Upward adjustment requires manual approval via `drift_alert` review (Slack/PR notification surface; manual platform-admin action)
- [ ] Exclude terminated-task rows from input distribution (closes the slow-skill positive feedback loop)
- [ ] Quarterly recompute thereafter

## Out of V1.0 scope (separate tracking issues to be filed)

- V1.5: heartbeat-with-phase, side-thread architecture, hang-threshold contract — separate issue once V1.0 ships
- V2: quality envelope schema enforcement, continueAsNew, hybrid A+B coordinator decomposition — separate issue once V1.0 has produced 30 days of compliance data
- V3: observed-p95 routing override, always-incomplete circuit breaker — deferred
- Subprocess adapter deprecation: separate 6-month tracking issue (RFC §"Subprocess adapters")

## Dependencies

- RFC #2251 — design source-of-truth (currently at v3)
- #2254 — Issue 4 reproduction harness
- #117 — `RuntimeCapabilities` dataclass (where `cleanup_grace_secs` lives)
- molecule-controlplane#302 — org_purges retry sweeper (prec

records.title: Observation chains have no traversal or accessor API, so downstream packages hand-roll reflective walkers
records.body:
An observation model is a nesting of modifiers around an error model, each holding the one it wraps in a field. That composition is the design and it works well. What is missing is any supported way to *inspect* or *update* the resulting chain, and the absence shows up in three distinct workarounds in `seabbs/EpiSewer.jl`.

## 1. A reflective walker, because there is no traversal

To compute how far back an infection series must start, EpiSewer.jl needs the total lead-in consumed by every `LatentDelay` anywhere in the chain. With no traversal API, it walks fields by reflection (`src/models.jl`):

```julia
_lead_in(::Any) = 0
_lead_in(d::LatentDelay) = _delay_length(d.delay) - 1 + _lead_in(d.model)
function _lead_in(obs::AbstractObservationModel)
    return sum(
        _lead_in(getfield(obs, f)) for f in fieldnames(typeof(obs)); init = 0
    )
end
_lead_in(branches::Union{Tuple, NamedTuple, AbstractVector}) = ...
```

That is a package reaching into `fieldnames` of another package's types. It works, and it has to handle `Split` branches separately, but it is guessing at a structure it has no contract for. Any wrapper that holds its inner model under a differently-shaped field breaks it silently — it returns a wrong number rather than an error.

## 2. Deep field paths in tests, which are brittle by construction

Reaching a specific component means writing out the nesting:

```julia
shedding = reverse(mdl.observation_model.model.model.model.delay)
```

Insert or remove a single wrapper and every such path in the codebase breaks, or worse, silently addresses a different component. There is no `find`-by-type to write instead.

## 3. Documentation has to explain the data structure

The EpiSewer.jl docs currently carry a paragraph explaining that the printed observation model shows only its outermost wrapper, that each wrapper holds the model it wraps in a field, and how to walk those fields to see the rest. A user reading a tutorial about wastewater modelling is being taught the library's internal representation because there is no other way to answer "what is actually in this chain".

## What would close it

Some combination of:

- **Traversal**: iterate or collect the wrappers of a chain in order, with `Split` branches handled. This is what `_lead_in` above actually wants — it would become a `sum` over a public iterator.
- **Find by type**: locate the `LatentDelay`s, or the innermost error model, without writing a field path.
- **Update by type or position**: replace a component in place, returning a new chain. This is the one users hit most. The natural idiom is `Accessors.@set`, but the lens path into a deep chain (`obs.model.model.model.error_model`) is as brittle as the field path, so it needs a lens keyed on something stable — type, or a name.
- **A `show` that prints the whole tree** rather than the outermost wrapper. R's EpiSewer prints its model as a tree of named parts and it is genuinely useful for checking what you built.

The update case is the one with the clearest user demand: swapping one component of a default model currently means rebuilding the entire chain around it, which is what EpiSewer.jl's tutorials have to demonstrate.

Happy to prototype whichever shape you prefer, since EpiSewer.jl has the reflective version working and would be the first consumer.

This was opened by a bot. Please ping @seabbs for any questions.

records.title: refactor(review): delete orphaned review authority after the SDD clean break
records.body:
## Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] The full #3417 and #3564 cleanup cluster was audited against current main.
- [x] Existing issues and pull requests were searched before reusing this approved tracker.
- [x] This issue is the non-SDD follow-up. #3564 owns the SDD clean break.

## Outcome

Delete every review/RDD production surface outside SDD that becomes orphaned after #3564 removes its final consumer. Retain only code with a named live path in the current atomic compact-v2 lifecycle.

This is deletion, not migration. Historical formats, versions, bindings, receipts, recovery shells, switches, and compatibility readers carry no lifecycle authority and are not recognized by the replacement implementation.

## Dependency

This work begins after #3564 lands its complete SDD cleanup. The post-#3564 source tree is the only valid reachability baseline. Pre-#3564 references do not justify retaining a provider whose final consumer is scheduled for deletion.

## Maintainer Decisions

### D1. No backward compatibility

Old review formats and authority representations are unsupported. A replaced version fails closed with one actionable instruction to start a fresh atomic review. There is no dual reader, compatibility translator, migration, record rewrite, or legacy fallback.

### D2. Preserve only the live atomic lifecycle

The retained review lifecycle is:

```text
candidate consent → freeze → admitted lenses → at most one bounded correction → targeted validation → approval and burn
```

Fresh STATUS/FINALIZE routing, exact consent, immutable candidate binding, reviewer admission, bounded correction, validator evidence, and terminal burn remain only when they are reachable from this lifecycle.

Approval leaves no terminal receipt, lineage, witness, tombstone, mirror, gate authority, or durable review history. Git remains the durable project history.

### D3. Delete by causal closure

When a consumer is deleted, delete its newly unreachable providers, direct tests, fixtures, schemas, help text, refusal continuations, ratchet entries, manifests, docs, and compile references in the same causal work unit. Do not baseline newly dead code and do not preserve a helper solely because a test calls it.

### D4. Evidence required for retention

Every retained review symbol must have all three:

1. a non-test production caller;
2. a named current compact-v2 scenario;
3. a focused test proving that scenario.

Anything missing one of these is deletion scope unless a separate approved issue owns a concrete current use.

## Scope

After #3564 merges, inventory and delete orphaned review/RDD code outside `internal/sddstatus`, including as applicable:

- retired review contract versions, schema fields, stores, receipts, bindings, lineage relations, selectors, projections, and compatibility translators;
- obsolete lifecycle switches, shadow observers, mirrors, gate evaluators, delivery interceptors, recovery shells, quarantine/repair paths, and maintenance verbs with no live compact-v2 transition;
- CLI/runtime adapter code that reconstructs retired review semantics instead of transporting the current native decision;
- tests, journeys, fixtures, assets, docs, prompts, help, refusals, ratchets, and OpenSpec assertions that preserve removed behavior;
- open issue and pull-request roots whose failure mechanism disappears with the deleted surface.

## Out of Scope

- The SDD cleanup owned by #3564.
- Deleting a compact-v2 operation that still has a reachable current transition and named test.
- Adding a replacement state, verb, flag, gate, mirror, or parallel authority representation.
- Release or publication work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A pinned post-#3564 inventory maps every non-test review/RDD symbol outside SDD to a current compact-v2 scenario or deletion.
- [ ] Every deleted surface includes its callers, tests, fixtures, schemas, help, refusal text, ratchet entries, and docs.
- [ ] No production code recognizes retired review formats or authority versions.
- [ ] No terminal review artifact survives approval and burn.
- [ ] Ordinary commit, push, pull request, release, and archive remain outside review authority.
- [ ] A universal architecture guard rejects reintroduction of retired versions, compatibility readers, terminal artifacts, and delivery gates.
- [ ] Guard decoys prove that mode, receipt, binding, witness, legacy, gate, recovery, and successor variants are detected.
- [ ] `go test ./...` passes at repository root, along with vet, format, refusal/dead-code ratchets, platform builds, and CI-equivalent driven review journeys.
- [ ] Remaining related issues and pull requests receive evidence-backed dispositions.

## Delivery Strategy

Use stacked-to-main, deletion-first slices by causal boundary. Each slice must be independently buildable and reviewable, and tests stay with the behavior they prove. If one causal deletion exceeds 400 changed lines, record the exact reason before applying `size:exception`; do not split a consumer from the providers that become dead because of its removal.

## References

- #3417
- #3564
- #3377
- #2471
- PR #3536
- PR #3567

records.title: maintain-wiki lint: detect capture files under raw/ that no page references
records.body:
## Problem

`maintain-wiki`'s `lint` verb checks the `<wikiDir>/` side of the bundle — dead wiki-links, orphaned pages, out-of-bundle links, staleness, and optional `raw/` immutability. It has **no check in the other direction**: a file under `<rawDir>/` that no page's `sources[].resource` points at.

That gap is silent and it accumulates. In `burbank-playfab`, a single branch added six capture files under `raw/`; **three of them (4,464 lines) are referenced by nothing at all**. Nothing in the audit, the gate, or `lint` reported it, and it was only found by hand-writing a grep during review.

It is the exact mirror of the **orphaned pages** check `lint` already performs — a page in no index — so the concept is already established in the skill; only the direction is missing.

## Why it matters more than ordinary dead weight

A capture is *supposed* to be immutable and permanent, so there is no natural moment at which anyone revisits one. Unlike a stale page, an unreferenced capture never surfaces:

- it is excluded from the hygiene scanners **by design** (`hygiene.excludePaths` includes `raw/`), precisely so its retired tokens and dead links are not reported;
- `lint`'s existing `raw/` check is about *immutability* (was it edited?), not *reachability*;
- captures are often large — whole-file snapshots of data or docs — so the cost per orphan is high. The three above averaged 1,488 lines each.

The net effect is a directory that only grows, where no tooling can distinguish provenance from litter.

## Proposed change

**1. Add an unreferenced-capture check to `lint`.**

Walk `<rawDir>/` recursively; collect every `sources[].resource` across `<wikiDir>/**/*.md`, resolve the relative ones against each page's own directory, and report any `<rawDir>/` file that nothing resolves to.

Advisory only, consistent with the rest of `lint` — it never fails, never exits non-zero. A capture may legitimately sit unreferenced for a while (captured now, ingested next session), so this is a report, not a defect.

Two details worth specifying so implementations agree:

- **Resolve, do not string-match.** Citations are relative (`../../raw/x.md`, `../../../raw/y.json`) and page depth varies, so a naive `grep` for the basename both over- and under-matches.
- **Report bytes or lines, not just paths.** The decision to keep or drop an orphan is almost entirely about its size.

**2. Consider a pre-commit hook** for consuming repos: block, or warn on, a commit that *adds* a file under `<rawDir>/` in the same tree where no `<wikiDir>/` page cites it. Catching it at the moment of creation is much cheaper than at review, and the check is the same resolver as (1).

A hook is more opinionated than `lint`, so it may belong behind a flag or as a documented opt-in recipe rather than something the plugin installs.

## Related, worth deciding at the same time

Two adjacent questions surfaced in the same review, both currently unaddressed by the schema:

- **What belongs in `raw/` at all.** The convention was written for retired docs and machine-local memory — sources git does not hold, or will not hold much longer. Applying it to files that are tracked and live in the same repo produces pure duplication: git already returns those bytes forever. A sentence in the schema template ("capture what git does not hold, or will not hold much longer") would have prevented the case above.
- **Whole-file vs excerpt.** A capture cited for one fact does not need the whole file — one of the orphans' cited siblings is a 3,375-line schedule captured to support a single date. Capturing the *relevant excerpt*, labelled with its source path and revision, keeps provenance while removing the bulk. It also sidesteps a real problem with the current guidance: the sanctioned origin form is a pinned `git:repo@<sha>:path`, but under a **squash-merge** workflow no branch sha survives, so a durable pin cannot be written until after the PR merges. An excerpt is frozen on its own and needs no sha.

Happy to supply the `burbank-playfab` case as a test fixture if useful.
